_: Prices, sinks and income (module 76 §124/§126). Gold's job is to feed training, services, potions and enchanting — not to be the reward itself (quests 00 §4).

potions._: Bought potions. Brewed ones are stronger for a skilled alchemist and cost only ingredients — deliberate (owner ruling: fixed difficulty binds the world, not the player's capacity to cope).

training._: One rank per session; never above the skill's governing attribute (reads base values). costPerRank * rank^exponent; retuned 2026-08-29 - at 15 x rank^1.15 training one skill to 100 cost more gold than the whole early economy produces.

income._: Gold REALISED from a cleared encounter. These are TEMPLATE drops - what the creature itself carries - because placed treasure never respawns (module 76 §126) and is counted separately as the content model's lootGoldPerHour. The first pass double-counted: every clear paid a full placed-loot value, and a 157-hour playthrough ended on 860,000 gold, which makes every sink meaningless. What a fight is WORTH as a piece of authored content is the ladder's own lootValue field; this is only what falls off the corpse.
